proposals.reasoning: Account-level 30d data: 83 add-to-cart events vs 15 purchases — roughly 68 people added to cart in the last 30 days without completing a purchase. Refreshed pixel-level check on 2026-08-29 (trailing 7d window, later same-day re-check) shows the pattern continuing and building: ~60 AddToCart events vs 11 Purchases (up from ~50 AddToCart earlier the same day — Purchase count unchanged at 11). Re-checked again this run (2026-08-29, event-level pull direct from the dataset): 50 AddToCart events vs 11 Purchases over the trailing 7 days — consistent with the same-day earlier reading, Purchase count still unchanged at 11. Refreshed once more this pass (2026-08-29, real-clock ~18:49 UTC, direct dataset-stats pull Aug22-29): 54 AddToCart events vs 12 Purchases over the trailing 7 days — both ticked up slightly from the prior 50/11 reading, same pattern continuing. Re-checked again (2026-08-30 daily run, direct event-level dataset-stats pull for the trailing 7-day window ending same real-clock time): 48 AddToCart vs 9 Purchase — within normal day-to-day fluctuation of the prior readings (48-54 AddToCart, 9-12 Purchase), same persistent gap. No retargeting campaign currently exists against this group. Rebuilt 2026-08-29 into a real, executable 4-step chain (previously only had 2 of 4 steps specced, with no real budget/creative/audience-rule values — approving it as originally written would have failed or produced an empty campaign shell). Uses the account's real active pixel ('Shopify Meta Pixel', dataset_id 833131719490535, last fired 2026-08-29) and the real Kage_Sales creative (id 1063318642863205, the account's best-ROAS creative at 4.30x, ad copy 'GRAB THE MOST CLICK-WORTHY SNEAKERS EVER').
proposals.actionSummary: 4-step chain, each step feeding the next real Meta-assigned ID (not guessed): (1) create the WEBSITE pixel audience — AddToCart OR InitiateCheckout in the last 14 days, excluding Purchase; (2) create the campaign (OUTCOME_SALES); (3) create the ad set targeting that new audience, India, Facebook+Instagram, optimizing for purchases, daily_budget 25000 (Meta's minor-currency-unit field — this is ₹250/day, editable via the parameter editor below, same conservative range as A-001's reactivation budget); (4) create the ad reusing the Kage_Sales creative. Every step is created PAUSED — approving this does NOT start spending. You'd review it in Ads Manager and activate manually, or tell Claude to activate once you're satisfied.

proposals.title: Launch a Dynamic Product Ads (DPA) campaign from the connected Shopify catalog
proposals.reasoning: A Shopify product catalog is already connected to this ad account (catalog_id 1149969713295773), but zero DPA/catalog-based campaigns are currently running. Gully Labs (main competitor) runs DCO/catalog ads as part of their active mix; KAI runs none. This is a structural gap, not a performance one. Meta's own Opportunity Score tool has been sliding across the last three runs on 2026-08-29 — 88 → 85 → 81/100 — and re-checked again this run at 81, still flagging Advantage+ catalog ads as a top recommendation (+4 points, 'lower cost per action'); a new offsite-conversion optimization recommendation (+5 points) also surfaced this pass, unrelated to the catalog gap. Catalog health check re-run on 2026-08-29 found the same 3 diagnostic issues, unchanged from the last check: 18 items still marked out-of-stock (must_fix — these won't appear in dynamic ads), 24 items with fewer than 2 images (opportunity), and 1 unmatched content ID between the catalog and pixel (opportunity). Rebuilt 2026-08-29 into a real chain: pulled live catalog product data (81 products total) and found no 'best-seller' field available via the catalog API — that framing was aspirational, not backed by real data, so downgraded to a defensible, real filter instead: in-stock only (availability=in stock), which also structurally avoids advertising the 18 out-of-stock items flagged above.
proposals.actionSummary: 3-step chain, each real: (1) create a product set filtered to in-stock items only; (2) create the campaign (OUTCOME_SALES, PAUSED); (3) create the ad set targeting India broadly with Advantage+ audience (matching the account's existing targeting_automation pattern on Kage_sales_1908), promoted_object pointing at the new product set, daily_budget 25000 (that's ₹250/day), PAUSED. Honest scope limit: the 4th step — the actual dynamic template ad (Meta's product-template creative format, distinct from a static image/video ad) — isn't wired into this automation's creative editor yet, which only builds static ads. Approving this proposal completes steps 1-3; the ad set will sit ready with its promoted_object set, and the final template ad needs one more manual step in Ads Manager (or a follow-up once template-creative support is built).

Page-matched Ad Library recheck (page_id 426015150606378, 'Lotto Sport India' confirmed as the matched page name): estimated_total_count is now 148 active ads, up from the last recorded 112 (+32.1%) — the first move to cross the module's 20% competitor-spike threshold across this account's several rescrapes today (prior moves were -1.7%, +6.7%, +1.9%, -11.2%, all below threshold). Gully Labs (page_id 107479854297817) also moved up this pass, 114 to 126 (+10.5%), still below threshold. Informational only — no proposal generated, this module never mutates the account. Worth a manual look at what Lotto Sport India is pushing (new collection launch, sale event, etc.) given the scale of the jump.

Update (2026-08-30, second daily pass, real-clock ~02:48 UTC): rechecked Lotto Sport India again — estimated_total_count is now 113 active ads, down from the 148 recorded above (-23.6%), itself a threshold-crossing move, just now in the opposite direction of the original spike. Gully Labs moved the same way this pass (126→86, -31.7%, see AL-015). Both pages dropping together, immediately after both had spiked together on the preceding scrape, reads more like Ad Library estimated_total_count sampling volatility than a genuine same-day swing in either competitor's live ad count. Treat both this reading and the original spike as noisy until corroborated by a manual look in Ads Library. settings.competitor_last_scrape has been updated to the fresh counts (86/113) so the next scrape compares against these, not the disputed 148/126.

Third pass (2026-08-30 daily run): rechecked again - Lotto Sport India is back to 148, exactly matching the original spike reading and reversing the -23.6% drop to 113. Combined with Gully Labs' identical round-trip (see AL-015 update), both pages have now bounced between the same two values three times in about a day (Lotto: 112->148->113->148). This is no longer plausibly two independent real-world ad-count changes on the same day - the module's estimated_total_count signal itself appears unreliable at this sampling frequency. Recommend requiring a move to persist across two consecutive scrapes before alerting, rather than alerting on every oscillation. No new competitor-spike alert filed for this bounce; settings.competitor_last_scrape updated to 148/126 for the next comparison.
